commands.label: Seal a dataset contract before it moves
commands.operator_goal: Name the dataset, its fields, and its hashes before a downstream lane treats it as normal.
commands.why_it_holds: Schema fingerprinting and catalog storage make type drift visible at the intake edge rather than during inference.
guardrails: Dataset fields are typed before they become batch assumptions.
Catalog writes happen before lifecycle or change-control records are accepted.

commands.label: Ingest rows through a named connector lane
commands.operator_goal: Move object-store or file-backed evidence into the replayable pipeline without flattening source provenance.
commands.why_it_holds: Connector configs, mappings, and persisted pipeline records stay coupled, which keeps the ingest story readable after the run.
guardrails: Connector benchmarks are stored with each run.
Pipeline events are sealed before replay claims are surfaced.

commands.label: Materialize a sound lane without storing the track
commands.operator_goal: Turn an audio reference into segments, derived features, embeddings, and receipts that can be queried later.
commands.why_it_holds: The manifest, segment index, feature vectors, and extraction receipts are versioned together, so the warehouse can change without becoming foggy.
guardrails: Raw audio is referenced, not committed into the repository.
Feature schema versions and extractor versions are stored with each run.

commands.label: Queue long-running multimodal work with receipts
commands.operator_goal: Keep batch work observable while preserving a typed request, a run journal, and replayable artifacts.
commands.why_it_holds: The batch route is smaller than a production cluster, but it still writes the receipt trail that a larger worker plane would need.
guardrails: Every submission yields a persisted job record.
The execution journal keeps command, duration, and status nearby.

commands.label: Re-run the same workload through many lanes
commands.operator_goal: Exercise ingest, replay, batch work, recipe compilation, and proof refresh under one reference workload.
commands.why_it_holds: The benchmark records stage durations and artifacts instead of timing one isolated function and calling that proof.
guardrails: Replay has to land on the same persisted frame chain.
Proof exports are refreshed from the backend edge, not typed by hand.

commands.label: Export a readable proof surface from the same runtime
commands.operator_goal: Give the frontend, the SDKs, and the repository pages one typed surface to read when the operator lane changes.
commands.why_it_holds: The operator bundle is exported the same way as the benchmark, music, and repository pulse surfaces, so it cannot drift into a separate narrative.
guardrails: Proof exports are generated by script and tracked in the journal.
Continuation links stay pointed at files that already exist in the repository.

commands.label: Evaluate a multimodal packet before it moves deeper
commands.operator_goal: Measure packet geometry, cross-border posture, and encrypted transport before downstream orchestration turns a weak packet into a stronger claim.
commands.why_it_holds: The gateway writes a ledger entry for every packet decision, so route, hold, and block actions do not disappear into ephemeral middleware.
guardrails: Cross-border packets can be blocked by jurisdiction profile.
Entropy-heavy or zero-heavy packets are held instead of quietly treated as normal.

skills.label: Schema fingerprinting
skills.focus: Keep upstream changes from silently mutating downstream assumptions.
skills.why_it_matters: Loose objects are easy to pass around and even easier to misunderstand. A contract lane slows that down before the model ever sees the payload.

skills.label: Music warehouse segmentation
skills.focus: Translate one audio reference into stable windows that can survive query, drift review, and cross-modal alignment.
skills.why_it_matters: A track average is too blunt. Segment-level memory lets the repository talk about where a pattern entered instead of only that it happened.

skills.label: Connector replay verification
skills.focus: Prove that the reconstructed run still matches the sealed frame chain after ingest.
skills.why_it_matters: Without replay, a connector story is mostly memory. Replay turns that memory into an audit surface.

skills.label: Bias and liability reading
skills.focus: Keep weak-signal drift, representational skew, and liability gaps close to the routes that produced them.
skills.why_it_matters: A bias taxonomy is only useful when it can still point back to the originating route, dataset, or warehouse segment.

skills.label: Generated client discipline
skills.focus: Keep SDKs downstream from FastAPI contracts so the typed edges stay aligned.
skills.why_it_matters: Generated clients keep the operator surface from being trapped inside the local Python service.

skills.label: Inspect, plan, run, and verify loop
skills.focus: Turn the current backend state into the next bounded improvement pass instead of waiting for a human to remember every loose edge.
skills.why_it_matters: Recursive capability only becomes respectable when the loop is grounded in real proof surfaces, not in self-congratulating text.

skills.label: Packet geometry gate
skills.focus: Use entropy, finite-value coverage, and zero-heavy ratios to slow a packet down before orchestration tries to make more of it.
skills.why_it_matters: The gateway lane makes packet quality visible at intake time, which is often earlier and more useful than blaming a later model output for weak source geometry.

plugins.label: Python client seam
plugins.purpose: Carry the runtime contract into notebooks, batch jobs, and local review tools without rewriting request shapes by hand.
plugins.guardrail: The client is generated from the same OpenAPI surface the backend serves.

plugins.label: TypeScript client seam
plugins.purpose: Keep browser and tooling surfaces typed when they call the backend.
plugins.guardrail: The `check` task fails if the generated surface drifts from the contract.

plugins.label: Compiled core bridge
plugins.purpose: Route hot signal math through the Rust crate when the lane needs lower-level profiling.
plugins.guardrail: The compiled core stays narrow and typed instead of swallowing the repository whole.

plugins.label: Proof export spine
plugins.purpose: Refresh the public proof files from the same backend routes the frontend reads.
plugins.guardrail: Artifacts are exported, logged, and verified rather than manually edited into place.

plugins.label: Recursive improvement seam
plugins.purpose: Keep the repository capable of reading its own route, proof, benchmark, and warehouse posture before the next repair pass begins.
plugins.guardrail: The loop only reads persisted proof and generated surfaces; it does not invent new capability claims outside those files.

plugins.label: Deployment stack seam
plugins.purpose: Keep object storage, event log, and analytics surfaces explicit enough to review without pretending the repository already operates a secret production cluster.
plugins.guardrail: The stack files stay versioned and inspectable, but they do not overclaim distributed control that the current backend has not yet earned.

speech_tasks.label: Speech presence audit
speech_tasks.focus: Separate spoken intervals from music-first or ambience-first windows without storing the waveform in git.
speech_tasks.why_it_exists: An audio lane becomes easier to question once speech-heavy and music-heavy segments stop being averaged into one posture.
speech_tasks.caution: The current lane derives this from feature windows and transcript presence; it is not pretending to be a hidden full-ASR service.
speech_tasks.next_step: Use this first when a reviewer needs to know whether language conclusions came from speech, chant, hooks, or dead air.

speech_tasks.label: Language share watch
speech_tasks.focus: Keep multilingual coverage visible while the lane is still shaped by instrumental.
speech_tasks.why_it_exists: Language drift often enters quietly through intake decisions rather than through the model itself.
speech_tasks.caution: Declared language coverage is only as honest as the manifest lane, so under-tagging should be treated as a real risk.
speech_tasks.next_step: Pair this with segment slices before making any claim about audience or regional reach.

speech_tasks.label: Caption and frame alignment trace
speech_tasks.focus: Follow one spoken or sung moment across transcript, segment window, and frame reference.
speech_tasks.why_it_exists: Cross-modal claims are much easier to trust when one moment can be located in time rather than described in averages.
speech_tasks.caution: The current alignment surface is strongest when transcript and frame references are actually supplied during extraction.
speech_tasks.next_step: Use this when a visual claim needs to stay accountable to the spoken record that traveled beside it.

speech_tasks.label: Silence and padding audit
speech_tasks.focus: Catch dead air, over-long intros, and presentation choices that masquerade as meaningful model evidence.
speech_tasks.why_it_exists: Silence is part of the story. It should be measurable before it quietly becomes a confound.
speech_tasks.caution: A calm signal is not automatically a weak one; this task is for spotting padding and imbalance, not punishing quiet material.
speech_tasks.next_step: Use this before retention or engagement stories are pinned to content rather than to editing posture.

speech_tasks.label: Chorus and repetition watch
speech_tasks.focus: Measure when a catalog narrows around repeated hooks, loops, or production habits rooted in signal-study, reference.
speech_tasks.why_it_exists: Repetition can be stylistic, commercial, or accidental. The important thing is keeping those meanings from collapsing together.
speech_tasks.caution: The repetition lane is descriptive first. It should help a reviewer ask sharper questions rather than jump to a verdict.
speech_tasks.next_step: Use this beside the drift cards when one sonic habit starts dominating a wider catalog conversation.
